lines.en: We returned straight to Seoul.
The first thing we checked was the [Industrial Complex]’s safety.
“No further unusual signs have been detected since then.”
Aileen, who was in charge of the central situation room, spoke.
Footage from around the Pacific was being broadcast on the situation room’s panels.
An enormous island that had risen in the Pacific beside the American continent. It was unmistakably one of the ‘disasters’ I knew.
In the main story of Ways of Survival, that island’s master had been a powerful Outer God. The question was whether it would be the same being this time.
“Where’s my mother?”
“On the east coast.”
“…The east coast?”
[The forgotten island is beginning to rise!]

Along with the system message, I saw waves surging from across the distant Pacific. Crustal movements on that scale would have sent immense tsunamis toward shores all over the world. Of course, the United States had suffered the most.
—Krrrraaack!

Amid the incarnations’ agonized screams, New York’s urban districts were being swept away. The tsunami wasn’t all. Beneath it swarmed the Nameless Ones, lower entities among the Outer Gods. These lower entities among the Outer Gods flooded in indiscriminately, gnawing away at the entire American mainland.

There was no time even to ask for aid. Less than thirty minutes after the disaster began, half the mainland had vanished. One hour into the disaster, the United States was covered in a pitch-black aura.
It was a disaster on a scale incomparable to the [Dark Castle] or the [Disaster of Floods] that had appeared in Seoul.
“Don’t tell me my mother…”
Aileen nodded and added,
“I’m not sure whether I should call it… fortunate.”

The next moment, the panel switched to the Korean Peninsula’s east coast. As expected, the tsunami had reached us too. The waves were lower than those that had struck the American mainland, and there were no Nameless Ones in sight, but the tsunami itself was still an enormous natural disaster.
—Heavenly Wind God!

At my mother’s cry, powerful winds burst from the folding fan at her fingertips. Pungbaek, who had been so obstinate during the Great War of Saints and Demons, seemed to be helping properly this time.
Cho Youngran, who could be called my mother’s right hand, was also fighting hard.
[The Giant Story ‘Shindansu’ begins its story!]
<Hongik> seemed to be watching the crisis too. Rooted in the sea, [Shindansu]’s Story was using the Korean Peninsula’s probability to hold back the disaster.
As though recovering from a terrible fright, Han Sooyoung muttered,
“…Wait, America. Isn’t that where that woman is?”
There was only one person Han Sooyoung would refer to as ‘that woman.’
“Couldn’t she predict this with Future Sight?”
“Actually, there’s something I need to tell you about that…”
Before Aileen could finish, a door on one side of the situation room opened and someone entered. The moment Yoo Joonghyuk recognized her, his hand went to the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword].
“I’m not here to fight, so put your sword away, Supreme King.”
The [Great Demon’s Eyes], pulsing with brilliant light.
The Prophet Anna Croft and Zarathustra, the group she led, stood there.
“I issued an alert five hours ago. Most people escaped to other parts of the world, but many couldn’t get out.”
“Why didn’t you ask us for help?”

“We didn’t even have the capacity for that. I couldn’t be sure of the information from Future Sight in the first place. This is the first time so much information about the future has changed so suddenly…”
Anna Croft looked bewildered.
A massive change in information about the future. It was probably evidence that, when it came to the final scenario, even Anna Croft’s Future Sight offered little advantage.
Han Sooyoung demanded,
“What about <Asgard>? After the successful conclusion of the Great War of Saints and Demons, they should have started supporting you again.”
Biting her lip hard, Anna Croft lowered her head and murmured,
“…They told me to abandon America.”
The final scenario would begin soon.
Perhaps even <Asgard> had no room to concern itself with one continent on a single planet.
After all, Earth wouldn’t be the only planet facing destruction.
An explosion rumbled from the panel.
【Kakakakakakakak】
【Weareweareweareweare】
The Outer Gods occupying the American coastline were howling.

I remembered Scenario 95, which I had experienced in the 1863rd round. In that worldline, the Outer Gods’ invasion had begun earlier than in ours. And now we would end up in much the same state. That was the story the damned Bureau wanted.
“…Does Korea have a plan?”
“I’m thinking about it.”
“I’ve heard you made contact with the king of the Outer Gods.”
She probably meant Secretive Plotter.
“To be precise, we’ve captured him.”
Anna Croft’s gaze wavered at my words. Apparently, she hadn’t known that much.
“Then… Could you perhaps use him to stop this disaster…?”
“He’s already exhausted too much probability. It’s impossible. Besides, he has nothing to do with this disaster.”
“You know something, don’t you?”
Instead of answering immediately, I met Anna Croft’s eyes.
If she wanted information, she had to cough up what she knew first. That was the basis of an information exchange.
Apparently understanding my intention, Anna Croft sighed softly and began.
“There isn’t much information I can give you.”
“Tell us what you can.”
“…First, the regions where the Great Apocalypse Scenario has activated are currently limited to part of the Pacific and the American continent.”
I already knew that.
[The Great Apocalypse is currently underway in that region.]

I saw a transparent dome stretching over the American continent and the entire Pacific. The Nameless Ones didn’t seem able to venture beyond its walls yet. That was probably the extent of the probability currently permitted to them.
“Second, the Nameless Ones can’t be hunted with ordinary weapons. Not only are conventional weapons systems ineffective, but even Star Relics from lower scenarios hardly work.”
Indeed, the screen showed several incarnations struggling desperately against the Nameless Ones.
One owned a fairly famous Star Relic, but his axe couldn’t properly cut their skin.
—Why…!
Flesh torn from an incarnation body by sharp teeth filled the panel. Lee Jihye grimaced and turned away. I watched closely without averting my gaze.
[The exclusive skill ‘Reading Comprehension’ activates!]
The carapaces surrounding the Nameless Ones’ bodies. I could see faint letters drifting over their surfaces. Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“A stigma.”
“Not just a stigma. If it can stay active like that, it’s already at the stage of a Visualised Story (形像說話).”
A Visualised Story. It was about time that much probability was permitted.
Yoo Joonghyuk nodded as though he agreed.
“The king of those Nameless Ones probably has an extremely powerful defensive ability.”
A king’s servants naturally followed their king’s Story. Just as Secretive Plotter’s Kkoma Yoo Joonghyuks had.
The Outer God that had raised an island in the Pacific was probably one of the five kings written of in the book left by the Recorders of Fear.
「The calamity of the western world, ‘Master of the Sunken Island.’」
I spoke reassuringly to my companions.
“Don’t worry too much. Constellations with higher Status should have weapons that can kill them.”
“But not a single constellation has joined the fight.”
Indeed, there were no constellations anywhere on the screen.
Not even one of the common Historical-grade constellations.
“We’ll have to start gathering them now.”
I glanced at Biyoo to use my True Voice. The channel was strangely quiet. Everyone must have seen that sight. And yet, no messages?
…Perhaps they were afraid of the king who had yet to emerge from deep beneath the sea.
“Jang Hayoung.”
Meeting my eyes, Jang Hayoung nodded.
If it was difficult to communicate with the constellations through the channel, borrowing Jang Hayoung’s strength was our best option. A little later.
“…No one’s replying.”
“No one?”
That couldn’t be. There were so many constellations in the <Star Stream>.
“The Black Flame Dragon was the only one to reply… He said he’s a little busy and can’t answer right now…”
“Did you try <Olympus> too? The <Underworld>?”
“First thing. But there’s no reply.”
Something was strange.
Leaving <Olympus> aside, surely the <Underworld> would respond.
And Uriel or the Great Sage, Heaven’s Equal…
Clicking her tongue beside me, Han Sooyoung said,
“Of course. That’s what constellations are really like.”
The modifiers of the constellations who had supported us passed through my mind one by one. There had been so many constellations, and not one would help?
Han Sooyoung continued.
“Plenty of constellations watched our Stories. Some cheered, some envied us. We got all kinds of reactions and earned plenty of coins. But that’s all.”
“Did you think our story had moved the world? That you’d really changed the <Star Stream>?”
“I wasn’t naïve enough to think that, but still…”
“Constellations only subscribe to channels that suit their tastes. They lost interest, so they moved to other channels. That’s all.”
I didn’t know whether Han Sooyoung was right.
[The next Great Apocalypse Scenario region is ‘Northeast Asia.’]
[14 days, 12 hours and 7 minutes remain until the Great Apocalypse Scenario begins.]
What was certain was that, with them turning away, the entire Earth might be blown away.
Jung Heewon asked,
“What do we do now?”
“…Well, this isn’t entirely unexpected.”
Han Sooyoung narrowed her eyes at me.
“Do you have a plan or something?”
“If they won’t come to meet us, we’ll go to them first.”
“Where will you start? The easy target, <Underworld>, I suppose?”
“You’re probably the only person who’d call the <Underworld> an easy target.”
I turned away from the sneering Han Sooyoung and looked at Jung Heewon.
Requesting aid from the <Underworld> was urgent, but something else was more urgent still. Fourteen days remained. We had to get the greatest results with the least travel.
“We need to get our missing companion back first.”
I looked at the steel sword hanging at Jung Heewon’s waist.
[The soul of the character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ is asleep.]
The aftereffects of Steel Transformation Stage 5 seemed more serious than I had thought.
“We’re going to meet the Master of Steel.”
“The Master of Steel? Will someone like that be any help?”
I nodded.
“He’s a powerful constellation. He isn’t Myth-grade, but right now, we need him more than we need a Myth-grade constellation.”
“Why?”
“There’s no time to explain the details. Let’s move.”

We needed an emergency contact and a minimal defensive force, so Jang Hayoung, Gong Pildu and Lee Seolhwa stayed at the Industrial Complex. I felt bad about leaving them behind again, but their expressions made me think that feeling that way was even more disrespectful. Come to think of it, Lee Seolhwa had said something similar.
“Hurry back. Leave this place to us.”
Staying in Seoul didn’t make their duties any easier.
Just as stories could only exist because there were things left untold.
We immediately boarded the [X-grade Ferrarghini] and entered the dimensional road.
The coordinates were OZ-7611. As the brilliant stars of the <Star Stream> flashed past, tension settled over my companions’ faces.
“There’s no need to be nervous. Just think of it as an outing… An extension of that workers’ revolution, or whatever it was.”
“…But we’re on the clock now.”
“I’m saying it because it isn’t such a frightening place.”
“Where are we going?”
“Well, as I said, to the Master of Steel’s home…”
“Who is he, anyway?”
Han Sooyoung finally asked in frustration.

“You can usually work out who other constellations are from their modifiers. The Prisoner of the Golden Headband is Sun Wukong, the God of Wine and Ecstasy is Dionysus. But I can’t guess anything about him. There wasn’t any information in the part I read, either.”
“If you’re curious, why don’t you figure it out with [Predictive Plagiarism]?”
“You want me to waste my ability on something so trivial?”
I shrugged.
Judging by their expressions, everyone—not just Han Sooyoung—was curious about the Master of Steel’s identity.
Jung Heewon asked,
“Is he someone from a myth we know?”
“He isn’t from a myth, but he’s an extremely famous constellation. There’s even a story based on his Story. Though… The children might not know it.”
At that, Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung looked glum.
Just as I was about to continue, a roar came from behind us.
“…Those bastards?”
Han Sooyoung, at the wheel, cried out in astonishment.
The silhouette of a battleship in the rearview mirror. Not just one or two. Dozens of space battleships pursued us, scattering ether particles.
Shin Yoosung asked,
“Aren’t those nebulae? Why are they attacking us?”
I wasn’t certain, but they looked like Story weapons from major nebulae such as <Vedas> or <Papyrus>. Lee Jihye frowned.
“Should I summon the turtle ship?”
“No. There’s no time to fight. Floor it, Han Sooyoung!”
We weren’t far from our destination anyway.
The [X-grade Ferrarghini] accelerated in the blink of an eye, tearing down the dimensional road at a breathtaking speed. Before long, a message appeared.
[You have arrived at coordinates ‘OZ-1900’!]
With a screech, the car stopped in midair. We had arrived at a station.
There was a small wooden house at the station. I shouted,
“Get out, quickly! Go inside that house!”
Almost the moment everyone entered the house, the [X-grade Ferrarghini] exploded.
…Damn it. I’d barely even ridden in it.
After making sure everyone was inside, I shut the front door. A terrifying tornado soon rose around the house. The house lifted off and began moving rapidly. I shouted,
“Lock all the windows!”
“Do you think locking the windows will stop that?”

Despite her protest, Han Sooyoung busily locked the windows. In the distance, the nebulae pursuing us were loading their guns. Dozens of battleships charging their photon cannons at once was a spectacle in itself. An attack like that could probably blow away the entire Korean Peninsula.
Lee Jihye cried urgently,
“Ajusshi! There’s still time to—”
“Don’t worry. We’re safe here.”
The entire house underwent a geometric transformation. Its interior expanded rapidly, and with an enormous metallic noise, pipes began growing throughout it.
“What? Wasn’t this a wooden house?”
[Beginning hull docking!]
The floating house locked into place somewhere with a clunk. At the same moment, a barrage fired from midair came pouring toward us. It was enough firepower to blow away a continent.
Just then, with a deafening exhaust noise, an unimaginably vast steel membrane began growing around the planet.
The incoming fire struck the membrane and vanished.
My companions looked at me, seemingly overwhelmed by the immense scale of the defensive barrier.
Through the window, I could see the contours of the planet where we had landed.
A silver city. An enormous planet that resembled a heart in contraction.
[Welcome to <Oz>, the Heart of Steel.]
<Oz>, the Heart of Steel.
The planet where the hardest metal in the <Star Stream> grew.
[The hull is entering stabilization.]
[Please wait.]
Hearing the system messages, my companions gazed blankly out the windows.
A house swept away by a tornado. A new world… By now, the others would probably have realized where we were.
“…Ajusshi, this is that story, right? 『The Wizard of Oz』.”
Surprisingly, Lee Jihye was the first to say it.
“You know it?”
“Yeah. A friend of mine used to like a musical based on it.”
The proud look on Lee Jihye’s face turned gloomy in an instant. Noticing, Jung Heewon quickly spoke up.
“But isn’t 『The Wizard of Oz』 a relatively recent work?”
“If I remember correctly, it was written in 1900.”
“Sangah-unnie really does know everything.”
Lee Jihye gave her a thumbs-up. Jung Heewon continued.
“But that doesn’t make sense. It’s a world barely a hundred years old… Hyunsung-ssi told me the Master of Steel was an older constellation than that.”
“You’re right, Heewon-ssi.”
It was a valid question. All Stories constituted beings. Since the Story making up that being was so young, of course she would wonder.
“What about 『Journey to the West』?”
“What?”
“Which came first? 『Journey to the West』 or the Great Sage, Heaven’s Equal?”
My companions looked as though they had realized something.
“So the Master of Steel might have existed before his story was told?”
“He might have. Or he might not.”
“What’s that supposed to mean?”
Exactly what I had said.
Once beings became Stories, their age grew less clear as time passed.
Even if a constellation had begun with a root Story, that root Story itself gradually changed with time.
[Hull stabilization is complete.]
[Opening the entrance.]
“Well, we’ll find out the details when we go out.”
Han Sooyoung was the first to hop down. An excited Lee Jihye and the children followed her.
“Let’s go too.”
The remaining companions nodded and disembarked.

If I remembered correctly, the scenario we would receive in <Oz> followed the original adventure exactly. A house carried away by a tornado arrived in the otherworld called <Oz>, and happened to crush an evil witch…
“What is this?!”
Then I heard Lee Jihye. She had probably discovered the witch beneath the house. But.
“…Isn’t this a fake?”
Someone was indeed crushed beneath the house. But it wasn’t a witch. It was a model shaped like a witch. A filthy model that barely even passed for one.
Holding up a broken mannequin leg, Han Sooyoung asked,
“What’s this?”
I stared at the leg.
「The plot has changed from the original.」
The planet <Oz> in Ways of Survival had been a kind of theme park.
Following the route of the original 『The Wizard of Oz』, visitors would meet the dwarfs known as Munchkins, each receive a role, and travel to the Emerald Castle.
But something was strange.
「There are no Munchkin dwarfs in sight.」
Yoo Joonghyuk murmured,
“It’s a little different from what my master told me.”
I agreed. What was I looking at?
A bleak wind blew through the silver city, where there was hardly any sign of life.
“It’s so desolate. For a fairy-tale world…”
Even after reading all of Ways of Survival, I didn’t know much about <Oz>.

<Oz> was only properly introduced once in the novel, during Yoo Joonghyuk’s 999th round. (The later parts of Ways of Survival skipped more and more scenes, until eventually it merely said things like, “He went to Oz and obtained Story metal to strengthen his weapons.”)
「What a sad place. I wish a happier tale could dwell here.」
I still clearly remembered those words from the Lee Hyunsung of the 999th round. It was here that he awakened his power and inherited the Master of Steel’s Status and will.
Yet no matter how I looked at it, this sight was completely different from the original.
Why? Because we had changed so much of the original?
But this was <Oz>. It wasn’t a planet strongly affected by the changes <Kim Dokja’s Company> had made.
“Shouldn’t fairy-like creatures come flocking over, singing and dancing as they guide us? Never mind fairies. There isn’t even a fly.”
A broken theme-park sign lay on the ground. It felt like an abandoned amusement park.
Even that seemed exciting to the children. They stuck close to me and murmured,
“It’s kind of like exploring a haunted house.”
For now, we decided to follow the yellow road marked on the ground. According to the original, the Emerald Castle stood at its end.
After walking a while, we did indeed see a tall green tower. A small city had formed around it.
「Since we have built an old castle where all journeys came to an end,」
「we hope you will gladly visit and remember our story.」
At the city’s entrance was an inscription that felt oddly sentimental.
That was when Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“I’ll go on my own from here.”
“What? Why?”
“There is an excellent blacksmith among the dwarfs here.”
His words brought a sentence to mind.
「The oldest magic dwells in the metal of Oz.」
<Oz> was the source of metal imbued with the oldest Story in the <Star Stream>. In the original, Yoo Joonghyuk’s weapon was strengthened with this place’s steel.
The strongest blade, reborn as a Star Relic by combining <Oz>’s metal with Yoo Joonghyuk’s Story.
That was the [Splitting the Sky Sword] Yoo Joonghyuk used in the latter part of the novel.
Of course, that was the original story. This time, he would probably strengthen the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword].
“Oz’s steel is the hardest in the <Star Stream>. Securing weapons is our priority now.”
With that declaration, Yoo Joonghyuk left without even asking permission. My companions looked at me as if asking whether it was all right to let him go, but I merely shrugged.
We had come to <Oz> for more than one reason, so we did need to split up. We didn’t need everyone to rescue Lee Hyunsung, either.
I spoke to Lee Jihye, whose eyes were shining beside me.
“Go with him. You need to upgrade your warship.”
“Yes!”
Lee Jihye trotted off excitedly.
I turned to Yoo Sangah.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi, could you secretly follow them too? I’m uneasy about sending those two alone. And the children… There should be plenty for them to see.”
“Hurry, let’s go! Hurry!”
Each child took one of Yoo Sangah’s hands, and they disappeared toward the shopping district. With the noisy group scattered, I felt a little empty.
Now, just me, Jung Heewon and Han Sooyoung.
Han Sooyoung murmured,
“That leaves Dorothy, the clever Scarecrow and the Cowardly Lion.”
There were four main members in 『The Wizard of Oz』: the protagonist Dorothy, the Tin Woodman, the clever Scarecrow, and the Cowardly Lion.
I asked,
“Since you specifically said ‘clever Scarecrow,’ I suppose that’s you.”
“Correct.”
“I won’t ask about the rest.”
“You’re the Cowardly Lion.”
“Thanks.”
Bantering, we entered the city center.
If this place were still a theme park, it would have been fun to form a party like that.
Shaking her head at us, Jung Heewon strode ahead.
Several groups of monkeys hid around the city, stealing glances at us.
They didn’t seem welcoming. A world without a welcome or anyone to greet us. It felt more like a horror novel than a fairy tale.
Before long, we reached the emerald tower. Han Sooyoung spoke.
“It looks just like a mage tower.”
“A wizard does live in it.”
Though I wasn’t sure if he still did.
We approached the tower’s entrance and knocked. A stiff male voice answered.
—State your business.
“We’ve come to see the Master of Steel.”
No answer came.
The door, still firmly shut.
Apparently, I had said the wrong thing. I thought back to Ways of Survival. What had they said in the 999th round?
While I was thinking, Jung Heewon drew her sword.
“Give Hyunsung-ssi’s soul back. Before I split your tower in half.”
An archangel’s Status, rising from her entire body. The moment the fierce flames of [Hell Flames Ignition] blazed over her steel sword, the door hesitantly opened.
[The Emerald Castle welcomes you.]
I wondered if this was really all right, but we were short on time anyway. It worked out well.
Seizing the opportunity, Han Sooyoung murmured with apparent admiration,
“That’s our Dorothy.”
“Shut up. I’m not here to play.”
Sidling over to me, Han Sooyoung whispered through [Midday Tryst].
—Scary as hell. Is that the power of love?
Jung Heewon, advancing as she swished the steel sword through the air. She had always been bold by nature, but seeing her like this, I was struck by how formidable her presence was.
—Seems like it.
The tower’s interior was plain. There were no particularly striking decorations, just the necessities placed where they were needed. Like the inside of Lee Hyunsung’s military backpack.

After about five more minutes of walking, we reached what seemed to be an audience chamber. We opened the door and entered. Brilliant lights came on, and a huge silver mask rose in the center of the room. Two empty eyes stared at us.
[<Kim Dokja’s Company>?]
A True Voice of steel, echoing throughout the audience chamber.
I knew at once. This was the Narrative-grade constellation Master of Steel, Lee Hyunsung’s sponsor. Probably his symbolic body.
“That’s right. It’s a pleasure to meet you.”
[So you are the Demon King of Salvation.]
I nodded. The silver mask regarded me with an annoyed gaze.
[What is the purpose of your visit?]
Straight to the point. Good.
“Please return Lee Hyunsung’s soul. I know you own it.”
[That is impossible.]
“Why?”
[His soul is necessary to maintain this planet.]
That was unexpected. When I turned, Jung Heewon was glaring at me. I quickly added,
“I know that’s how those damned sponsor contracts work, but Hyunsung-ssi is our companion. I thought you liked our story too.”
“And doesn’t <Oz> already have more than enough Giant Stories? There should be no reason to use Hyunsung-ssi’s soul as a power source.”
『The Wizard of Oz』 was a Story famous enough to be known even on Earth. Its popularity had faded these days, but it had once taken the entire world by storm.
If it was that famous on Earth, how much more so in the <Star Stream>? In other words, there should have been no shortage of power.
Even so, the Master of Steel was adamant.
[Go back. I cannot return the soul.]
“If you really need power, trade his soul for our Stories. We’ll supply you with Stories you can use for power.”
[I told you to go back.]
Yes, something was strange. If he merely wanted to use Lee Hyunsung for power, there was no reason to refuse my offer.
“I’m sorry, but we must take his soul back. The final scenario is about to begin. This is no time to concern yourself solely with your own safety.”
[The Story ‘Demon King of Salvation’ begins its story!]
As I released my Status, the Master of Steel seemed flustered.
[You dare oppose me here in <Oz>?]
Sparks crackled through the audience chamber. The Master of Steel was a Narrative-grade constellation.
And according to the original, here in <Oz> alone, his Status—
[Merely allowing you inside was an act of goodwill…!]
was comparable to a Myth-grade constellation’s.
Rrrrummble!
The planet writhed violently, like a heart repeatedly contracting and relaxing.
Han Sooyoung looked at me, pale.
—Kim Dokja, are you insane? If you fight here, how are we supposed to…
I released my Stories.
[The Giant Story ‘Demon Realm’s Spring’ begins its story!]
[The Giant Story ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’ begins its story!]
As our main Giant Stories began, the audience chamber shook as though it would collapse at any moment.
I stepped forward through the fierce tremors. The Master of Steel shouted,
[Step back! If you do not step back…!]
Just as I thought.
Despite having had more than enough time to subdue me, the Master of Steel merely repeated his warnings without taking any action.
Just like a cowardly lion.
I walked straight through the mask and reached the wall at the rear of the audience chamber. The Master of Steel was shouting something. Ignoring him, I punched the wall.
The next moment, the silver mask floating like a hologram vanished.
“Hey, monkey.”
Beyond the hole in the wall, a terrified monkey was trembling.
“Where’s the real Master of Steel?”
A little later, we had extracted information from the monkey. Han Sooyoung spoke.
“So the Master of Steel isn’t here.”
[I-if you lot do this, the Master of Steel’s forgiveness…]
“Turn off the True Voice switch. It doesn’t even sound like a True Voice.”
“…is probably what you’ll receive.”
The monkey spoke dejectedly.
This monkey was probably the Master of Steel’s close attendant. I didn’t know why, but he had been living here pretending to be a constellation.
“Then you’re the one who’s been sending all those indirect messages?”
“Y-yes. But I made sure they reflected the Master of Steel-nim’s wishes.”
“Reflect his wishes?”
At my question, the monkey looked toward the edge of the audience chamber. An enormous steel sword stood embedded in an altar there, like a cross.
I examined the sword’s appearance closely.
“Originally, we could hear the Master’s wishes through that altar. But contact suddenly stopped recently…”
I placed my hand on the altar’s steel sword. A tingling sensation ran through me. I had experienced that feeling before.
Faint though it was, this was unmistakably the sensation of touching another worldline.
Which meant the Master of Steel was a being from another worldline.
…But that couldn’t be. As far as I knew, the Master of Steel was the Tin Woodman from 『The Wizard of Oz』… Had someone else plundered his constellation name?
While I was lost in thought, Han Sooyoung asked,
“Does that have something to do with the state your planet’s in?”
“…Partly. Neglect is also a problem. All Stories eventually decline. It has been a long time since magic disappeared from <Oz>. Do you even know how old this place’s Story is?”
“No.”
“Tourists no longer visit <Oz>. It has already been three years since our monthly average visitor count hit double digits.”
A distant look filled the monkey’s eyes, as if recalling former glory.
“Once, <Oz> was one of the greatest theme parks in the <Star Stream>…”
Jung Heewon frowned.
“That’s not what we want to hear. Are you giving Hyunsung-ssi’s soul back or not?”
“Th-that’s a little…”
“Why?!”
“Because it’s thanks to that Lee Hyunsung that we can maintain even a double-digit visitor count.”
“What on earth does that mean?”
After hesitating a long time, the monkey spoke.
“Do you know that the influence of old Giant Stories has been weakening recently?”
“Giant Stories’ influence is weakening…?”
“It isn’t just <Oz>. Many Stories that made up existing Giant Stories are declining in much the same way as <Oz>.”
“Why?”
“Because a certain Story that recently rose to prominence has begun eating into the other Stories’ shares.”
The monkey raised his head and looked at me resentfully.
“Your Story.”
To get straight to the point, our visit to the Emerald Castle hadn’t been entirely fruitless. The monkey had said,
—You may take Lee Hyunsung with you. In return, please help promote <Oz>.
When we asked how, he had replied,
—You’ll know once you go where Lee Hyunsung is.
That was why we were here now.
In the distance stood a Ferris wheel that no longer turned and a decrepit merry-go-round. A textbook example of a completely ruined theme park.
《There Is No Wizard in Oz》
Apparently, that had been the theme park’s name. A rather stylish one.
The problem was the subtitle beneath it.
《But There Is Lee Hyunsung》
—Lee Hyunsung’s ‘Memory Experience Center’ is now open!
—Find Lee Hyunsung’s soul hidden somewhere in the center to receive a small prize.
…What on earth was this?
A price list awaited us at the ticket booth.
●Admission ticket: 4,000 coins
●Unlimited pass (50% discount): 3,000 coins
They were practically telling us to buy the unlimited pass.
The ticket seller asked,
—How many are entering?
“Three.”
—3,000 coins per incarnation. 60,000 coins for a constellation.
…Had I heard that wrong?
While I stood stunned by my first taste of such merciless discrimination, Jung Heewon held out her hand to me.
“We can charge this to the company, right? It’s a mission.”
“…Of course.”
“One incarnation ticket, please.”
Jung Heewon casually swiped the company card and entered the ‘Memory Experience Center.’ While I stood there in a daze, Han Sooyoung stepped forward too.
“One incarnation ticket here—”
“Wait.”
“What? Why?”
“There’s a discount plan.”
I pointed at the small notice beside the price list.
●Introducing the Constellation X Incarnation Couple Discount Ticket!
●A couple discount ticket for sponsors visiting with their own incarnations! Make beautiful memories with your incarnation and enjoy a sweet, cozy time together!
Having read it all, Han Sooyoung looked at me. I nodded. She asked,
“Are you insane?”
“No matter how many coins I have, I don’t have any to waste here.”
Glaring furiously at me, Han Sooyoung counted on her fingers as though calculating something. Then she glanced once at the price list and once at me, sighed, and asked,
“What will you give me?”
“…What are you two doing?”
Jung Heewon asked when she spotted Han Sooyoung and me. Understandably so: we were wearing identical wolf-ear headbands.
[This item cannot be removed while you remain in the ‘Memory Experience Center.’]
[Show off the close bond between you and your incarnation to the other constellations!]
Han Sooyoung answered shamelessly.
“I’m working a part-time dating gig.”
“Let’s find Hyunsung-ssi first.”
If the monkey was right, Lee Hyunsung’s soul would be roaming freely somewhere inside this ‘Memory Experience Center.’ I didn’t know why on earth he was wandering around a place like this…
We still had time, so we calmly explored the ‘Memory Experience Center.’
I had wondered what a Memory Experience Center could be, but soon found out.
[Lee Hyunsung is born a healthy baby weighing a whopping 5.4 kg!]
[Five-year-old Lee Hyunsung saves a friend from bullying!]
This was a place to experience Lee Hyunsung’s life.
[Only ‘unlimited pass’ holders may enter.]
[A possession experience begins upon entry. Would you like to enter?]
“So if you go in here, you can find out what it’s like to be a big, healthy baby? Who pays to experience crap like this?”
The theme park resembled an amusement park.
In each attraction, we could experience life as Lee Hyunsung or someone around him. Jung Heewon said,
“We really must have become famous, if they’re making things like this.”
“…I’m curious about that one.”
Before we knew it, we were absorbed in looking into Lee Hyunsung’s life. I truly felt like a constellation. …Come to think of it, I really was one.
[Seventeen-year-old Lee Hyunsung’s heart-pounding first love ends in failure!]
Jung Heewon stared at that attraction for a long time. I asked,
“…Do you want to go in?”
“No.”
We continued searching for Lee Hyunsung.
Lee Hyunsung’s soul had a distinctive Story reaction. I was certain I could clearly sense it nearby, and yet…
[Lee Hyunsung meets the Judge of Evil!]
As we kept walking, we found attractions connected to <Kim Dokja’s Company> too.
[Pure-Hearted Steel Lee Hyunsung! The Judge of Evil…]

Jung Heewon walked faster and faster. We hurried after her. But there was no sign of Lee Hyunsung. After checking a whole row of attractions, we turned back—and someone was there. It wasn’t Lee Hyunsung.
“Oh? Ajusshi?”
It was Lee Jihye, wearing a fox-ear headband.
“…Why are you here?”
At my question, Lee Jihye gave a simple explanation.
How she had taken Yoo Joonghyuk, Yoo Sangah and the children to the smithy, only to find it had run out of Story metal.
How they had wandered around dejectedly and happened upon this place.
And how the children’s pestering had forced them to enter on a ‘family discount’… A family discount?
“What are you doing here?”
I turned to find Yoo Joonghyuk there too, wearing a fox headband. Looking between Han Sooyoung and me, he asked,
“Have you recovered Lee Hyunsung’s soul?”
“We’re here to look for him. What are you doing here instead of finding Story metal?”
“The blacksmith’s shop was closed. They said they had run out of Story metal.”
I thought I knew why that had happened. Perhaps it too was related to the weakening of <Oz>’s Giant Story.
Yoo Sangah, waving toward us from a distance. I could also see Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung wearing headbands that resembled dragonfly wings.
“Unnie, let’s go in there next! There!”
“Oh my, that one’s for ages eighteen and up.”
Just like that, everyone had gathered again.
I decided it was just as well. Since things had turned out this way, searching for Lee Hyunsung together would save us some trouble.
That was when I heard Jung Heewon.
“Everyone, come over here!”
We went straight toward her.
There stood an attraction with far more warnings than the others.
●This attraction is only available to visitors aged eighteen or older.
●Those participating in the possession experience may suffer psychological distress due to abuse.
●Caution is advised for male-bodied incarnations from Korea.
Looking up at the attraction’s name, I said,
“…I think we’ve found him.”
There was no doubt. Lee Hyunsung’s characteristically dull, slow Story was clearly emanating from this attraction.
Lee Hyunsung was inside.
I raised my head and read the attraction’s name.
[I Lost a Cartridge Case by Mistake]
“Hyunsung will do well.”
“Hey, it’s not too late. Tie plastic bottles to your legs and jump from the third floor.”
“Everyone goes. Come back a decent human being.”
The sort of ordinary remarks anyone heard before enlisting, as ordinary as his life.
A life spent constantly trying to follow everyone else’s lead.
Like everyone else, he sang ‘A Private’s Letter’ and enlisted alone, without a best friend or girlfriend to see him off at the training camp.
“Recruit Number 53.”
“Recruit Number 53, Lee Hyunsung!”

At first, Lee Hyunsung’s military life wasn’t bad. Thanks to his naturally tall stature and well-developed muscles, he was even recommended for the role of trainee battalion leader. If he hadn’t kept getting the battalion leader’s oath wrong, he might have graduated from training with a commendation.
“Recruit, do you think your drill instructor is joking?”
He had known since childhood that he was slow.
Whatever he did, he learned more slowly than others and wasn’t quick to read a situation.
Even so, he had managed to get by because there were people who liked his easygoing, steadfast nature.
But there were no such people in the army.
“Of all people, I had to get that bastard as my buddy…”
“He’s just fucking huge and nothing else…”
Amid one insult after another, Lee Hyunsung endured his time as a recruit.
By the time he finished training, he had become the sort of person who could shower in five minutes and tidy his bedding in one.
Before long, the time came for his unit assignment.
Lee Hyunsung had been waiting for that moment ever since enlisting.
—Tips for new recruits. Here’s what to do when you’re assigned to a unit. (Hot!) [812]
From insoles for marches to ways of winning his seniors’ affection after his unit assignment. The military tips he had studied online the day before enlisting were what gave him hope.
One by one, his fellow recruits left for their units.
The person who came for him, the last recruit left, was someone called Sergeant First Class Jung. A fatigue cap pulled low obscured Jung’s face.
“You’re coming with me.”
As he rattled along in a military truck, Lee Hyunsung thought about his life again. He thought about the little more than two years that lay ahead of him, and the trials to come.
The unit was halfway up a small mountain. At last, his real military life was beginning.
With a member of the unit’s staff guiding him, he completed the brief registration process for new recruits and headed to the barracks.
And the moment the barracks door opened wide.
—You absolutely have to do this.
Lee Hyunsung put the tip he had read online into practice.
“Your new recruit’s here—!”
In an ordinary army, Lee Hyunsung’s military life would have ended there.
In an ordinary army, that is.

The moment Lee Hyunsung threw his duffel bag into the air, everything slowed as if in slow motion. The duffel bag slowly coming undone in midair. Grimy army-issue underwear, toilet paper, the soap he had used at training camp and the like were scattering very slowly, like a burst of bullets. And there was Lee Hyunsung’s triumphant face, brimming with hope for life in his unit…
In a scene like a film on the verge of tragedy, someone asked,
—…What should we do?
Someone else answered,

—We can’t help it. That’s Hyunsung-ssi for you. Anyway, let’s accept reality too. We failed last time with the abuse version, so for this branch, we’ll use the progressive military culture concept, as promised…
—Shut up and get started, Kim Dokja.
—…Then let’s begin again!
And the scene began moving again.
Thud!
His duffel bag, launched like a cannon shot, burst across the barracks floor like a shell.
The atmosphere gone cold, as though doused with cold water. His seniors’ gazes belatedly fixing on him.
Cold sweat slowly beaded along Lee Hyunsung’s back. Had something… gone wrong?
Then, the next moment.
Sergeant First Class Jung, who had brought him here, smiled and clapped.
“Laughter exercises, begin! Hahahahaha! Wow, that was fun! I’ve never seen such a fresh debut!”
As if they had been waiting, the seniors in the barracks rose in a standing ovation.
“New recruit-nim! That was truly amazing!”
“Impressive.”
Amid the scattered applause, Lee Hyunsung felt triumphant again despite his bewilderment. He had done it. The tip had been right. Sergeant First Class Jung addressed the soldiers.
“Joonghyuk, you’re his immediate senior. Look after him.”
“…Understood.”
Amid the commotion, Lee Hyunsung noticed a senior tidying the things on the floor for him.
A sharply pressed uniform. Bright, piercing eyes and a sculpted face.
On his chest were private first class insignia and the name ‘Yoo Joonghyuk.’
So this is my immediate senior.
At that moment, his immediate senior’s terrifying gaze turned toward him.
“P-Private Lee Hyunsung!”
“Your place is over here.”
His belongings, already tidied, were placed on top of the locker.
The seniors exclaimed in admiration, saying they had expected nothing less.
“New recruit, watch and learn. Joonghyuk’s our unit’s ace.”

Their attitudes alone made it clear what sort of person his immediate senior was. A perfectly shaped beret and crisply folded bedding. Everything he touched seemed to shine. If only he could serve like this man…
“What’s this? A new recruit?”
Just then, a cheerful voice came from the entrance. A face slick with sweat, perhaps from just coming off duty. Catching a glimpse of sergeant insignia, Lee Hyunsung hurriedly saluted.
“Loyalty!”
“Oh, don’t be so nervous. At ease.”
Looking at Lee Hyunsung’s face, the sergeant smiled, then turned toward Private First Class Yoo Joonghyuk.
“Our Joonghyuk’s got it damn easy, huh? An immediate junior already?”
The man’s sneering face was far too pale for a soldier’s.
Why was it that, the moment Lee Hyunsung saw him, he felt an ache deep in his chest?
Recognizing the man, the soldiers shouted,
“Sergeant Kim Dokja-nim! Have you returned from duty?”
“Yeah. Why isn’t Joonghyuk greeting me?”
“…Wel…come…ba…”
Private First Class Yoo Joonghyuk was trembling, his face white. It seemed contorted with rage rather than fear.
Watching him, Sergeant Kim Dokja shrugged and spoke.
“Welcome to our squad, Lee Hyunsung.”
“Private Lee Hyunsung!”
That was Lee Hyunsung’s first meeting with Squad Leader Kim Dokja.
…Within Lee Hyunsung’s memories, that is.
Before he knew it, two weeks had passed since his unit assignment.
In that time, Lee Hyunsung had learned various things about the unit.
For instance, Sergeant Kim Dokja, who held the real power in his squad.
“Understand? If that bastard Yoo Joonghyuk mistreats you, tell me right away.”
“P-Private Lee Hyunsung! Nothing like that has happened!”
“No, it will. You’ve already been through plenty.”
“…Pardon?”
And Private First Class Yoo Joonghyuk, who always led by example right beside him and glared at Sergeant Kim Dokja at every opportunity.
“This is how you polish your boots.”
“P-Private Lee Hyunsung! I’ll do my best!”
“Doing your best is meaningless. What matters is doing it well.”
First Lieutenant Yoo, the nursing officer who occasionally came for health checks.
“Hmm, your leg’s bruised. …Shall I get you medically discharged?”
“P-Private Lee Hyunsung! I’m perfectly fine!”
“Then shall I stitch it up? I’m good with thread.”
Sergeant First Class Jung, seemingly casual yet attentive, who sometimes looked at him with sad eyes.
“…Are you managing okay?”
“P-Private Lee Hyunsung! I’ll do my best!”
“You don’t have to. You always do.”
All of them were strange in one way or another.
“For our unit to establish a progressive military culture!”
But if one person was the strangest of all.
“All soldiers must read webnovels during personal time. Reading webnovels is the alpha and omega of personal upkeep.”
It was Captain Han, the company commander.
“That is all! Personal time begins shortly! Everyone, read webnovels.”
“Loy! Alty!”
And so Lee Hyunsung’s dreamlike military life began.
But Lee Hyunsung didn’t know.
[<Kim Dokja’s Company> is currently attempting the Memory Experience Center attraction ‘I Lost a Cartridge Case by Mistake.’]
[This attraction’s difficulty is Extreme (極上).]
[Number of clear attempts so far: 3.]
That this was not, in fact, his first time living this military life.
As you can probably tell without an explanation, five of us were participating in this scenario.
Myself, Yoo Joonghyuk, Yoo Sangah, Jung Heewon and Han Sooyoung.
For reference, this was the hidden scenario we had received.
<Hidden Scenario—I Lost a Cartridge Case>
Classification: Hidden
Difficulty: ???
Clear conditions: The incarnation ‘Lee Hyunsung’ is trapped in his own memories. Resolve his trauma and rescue him from those memories.
Time limit: ???
Reward: Lee Hyunsung’s return; major rewards may be received for raising awareness of <Oz>.
Failure: Accelerated destruction of <Oz>.
It was a ridiculous scenario. The question marks for the time limit were troublesome enough, but the clear conditions and failure penalty were even more bewildering.
Sergeant First Class Jung Heewon-nim… No, Jung Heewon asked,
“Sergeant Kim Dokja.”
“Yes.”
“Never mind the rest. Why on earth does <Oz> get destroyed if we fail?”
“I have two hypotheses. One is that awareness of <Oz> has dropped that far… The other is that this could point to some sort of physical crisis.”
With a boom, a faint tremor echoed from beyond the sky. I thought of the nebulae that had pursued us here. Perhaps they had begun a full-scale invasion. If so, we didn’t have much time left.
Perhaps he had heard the rumbling. Lee Hyunsung came running toward us from a distance, his face deathly pale.
“Sergeant Kim-nim!”
“Oh, Hyunsung.”
“I think North Korea’s attacking!”
“It’s all right. Go rest.”
“Loyalty!”
Wandering as if he didn’t know what to do, Lee Hyunsung eventually went to a corner of the base and began practicing the armed forces’ calisthenics, which he had yet to memorize.
Watching him, Jung Heewon murmured,
“Will Hyunsung-ssi really be able to come back?”
“I don’t know either. We’ll have to try.”
This was already our third attempt.

We had failed on the first attempt because many of our companions knew little about the military (I was the only one who had completed military service), and on the second because of Yoo Joonghyuk’s abuse.
Frowning beside me, Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“How frustrating. Lee Hyunsung wakes up faster if you push him hard. Have you forgotten our experience in Kaizenix?”
“We tried that on the second attempt.”
“I can do better if I try again.”
“You know perfectly well that isn’t true.”
“You know saving someone can’t be that easy.”
Yoo Joonghyuk had lived through three rounds… Perhaps as many as 1,864. In truth, he would know that without me saying it.
“Lee Hyunsung! Your exercise sequence is wrong!”
…Or perhaps he didn’t.
Yoo Joonghyuk, striding toward an alarmed Lee Hyunsung.
Watching the two do the armed forces’ calisthenics side by side, I spoke to Jung Heewon.
“We shouldn’t stay here too long. Yoo Joonghyuk’s acting strange too.”
“…Strange?”
“He’s never even been in the military, but he’s adapting far too well.”
I watched Yoo Joonghyuk perform calisthenics with near-maniacal precision.
In the 144th round, Yoo Joonghyuk had once gone mad after receiving an improper transfusion of Lee Hyunsung’s ‘military Story.’
If more time passed and another Story like 「Mad Soldier Yoo Joonghyuk」 was created… Jung Heewon spoke.
“Isn’t it good that he’s adapting well?”
“He’s adapting well, but he treats me, his senior, disrespectfully. The army’s really gotten soft these days. Back in my day…”
“Dokja-ssi, you’re just upset Joonghyuk-ssi didn’t serve, aren’t you? He was exempt.”
I answered calmly.
“…Anyway, aside from that, things aren’t so bad. Just having us here is raising awareness of the planet <Oz>.”
[Many constellations are currently paying attention to this scenario!]
Perhaps word had spread that <Kim Dokja’s Company> was creating another bizarre Story. Visitors to Biyoo’s channel increased.
I didn’t know for sure, but the nebulae targeting us outside the planet were probably watching too. If we couldn’t avoid being targeted anyway, we might as well use the situation itself.
[Many constellations have entered the channel!]
[The planet <Oz>’s fame is spreading widely!]
[A new Story related to the incarnation ‘Lee Hyunsung’ is sprouting!]
What was strange was that the newly arrived constellations weren’t the ones I knew.
Uriel, the Great Sage, Heaven’s Equal, the Abyssal Black Flame Dragon, Goryeo’s First Sword… Those familiar modifiers had vanished like an ebbing tide.
An ominous feeling came over me. Had something happened to them?
[Some constellations look forward to the return of the incarnation ‘Lee Hyunsung’!]
We would have to resolve this scenario quickly before we could find out anything.
“Do we really have to resolve it?”
“What?”

Without answering, Jung Heewon looked at Lee Hyunsung. Under Yoo Joonghyuk’s guidance, he continued his exercises, drenched in sweat. Perhaps he had performed the sequence correctly: Yoo Joonghyuk nodded. Lee Hyunsung’s delighted face.
[The character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ is happy!]
“He’s always going on about manuals, so I thought Hyunsung-ssi was a born soldier.”
I had thought the same, so I nodded.
Even Ways of Survival didn’t cover Lee Hyunsung’s earlier life in such detail.
Lee Hyunsung, the man who lived and died by the manual. In truth, no one had been farther from that manual than him.
This was the world where Lee Hyunsung’s manual had been born.
[The character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ likes this place.]
Jung Heewon smiled weakly and spoke in a sad voice.
“Maybe we’re just being selfish by trying to take him away.”
Perhaps Lee Hyunsung would be happier in <Oz>.
Perhaps he would be better off spending his time peacefully in his memories than wandering through hellish scenarios.
Rrrrummble…
That was when another roar sounded.
As I met Jung Heewon’s eyes, channel messages appeared one after another.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ enters the channel!]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ enters the channel!]
[The constellation ‘Goryeo’s First Sword’ enters the channel!]
The vanished constellations were returning to the channel all at once.
Just as I was about to ask what had happened.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’—a danger signal for you…!]
Ssssspark.
[The use of all indirect messages within the channel is restricted.]
The indirect messages cut off.
When I looked up, Biyoo looked startled. Naturally, she hadn’t done it. …Then who?
Another roar echoed from the sky. With a sound like an enormous drum being torn apart somewhere unimaginably distant, cracks spread through the heavens.
Crrrraaack.
“…Dokja-ssi.”
Something was going wrong.
